info.bio:
Duane Eddy es un guitarrista de rock'n'roll americano, nacido en Corning en el estado de Nueva York, el 26 de abril de 1938.
Popularizó el famoso sonido de guitarra eléctrica "twang", inspirado de la música country & western, obtenido sustituyendo las cuerdas graves del instrumento por las de un bajo, y una reverberación muy amplificada. Pariente pobre de este estilo, su influencia en el rock y el pop no es sin embargo desdeñable. Fue redescubierto en los años 1980 gracias a un muestreo del tema de Peter Gunn por el grupo Art of Noise.

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

podcast.title: Death Details - April 30, 2024
podcast.body: Duane Eddy died on April 30th, 2024, at the age of 86. His cause of death was cancer. "On April 30th, Dwayne Eddy died of cancer at age 86."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cover of "Honky Tonk"
podcast.body: Dwayne Eddy, known for his instrumental style, recorded a cover version of Bill Doggett's "Honky Tonk." His entire musical style appears to have been derived from the influence of this particular song. "And indeed, Dwayne Eddie's whole style seems to have come from Honky Tonk."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Guitar Rock Pioneer
podcast.body: Duane Eddy was a pioneering figure in guitar rock during the 1950s, known for his distinctive twangy guitar sound. This sound was instrumental in underpinning the emerging surf rock genre. "He was a guitar rock pioneer for the 1950s with a twangy sound that underpinned the rising surf rock sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Key Musicians
podcast.body: Eddy's unique guitar style had a significant impact on other prominent musicians, including George Harrison and Bruce Springsteen. "He was a big influence on George Harrison and Bruce Springsteen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Phil Harvey Band
podcast.body: The Phil Harvey band's concept incorporated Dwayne Eddy's style of rock guitar instrumentals, blending it with complex jazz. "The band's concept was apparently a mix of Dwayne Eddy's style rock guitar instrumentals and complex jazz, with the group All Dressed As mobsters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Last Surviving Billboard Hot 100 Top 10 Artist
podcast.body: Upon his death, Duane Eddy was the last surviving musician who had achieved a top 10 hit on the very first Billboard Hot 100 singles chart, which debuted in 1958. "When he died of cancer at age 86, he was the last surviving musician to have had a top 10 hit on the first ever Billboard Hot 100 singles chart in 1958."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Produced by Sill & Hazelwood
podcast.body: This record was one of a few hits produced by the team of Sill and Hazelwood, who later took over some production duties for The Coasters. "Stull and Hazelwood had recently had a few hits of producing records like Vappel Rouse and Byteway and Addy."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Twist Record (Year?)
podcast.body: Duane Eddy also recorded a twist record during the period of the twist craze. Many of these contemporary twist records were described as being of low artistic merit. "There were twist records by Bill Haley, Neil Sedarka, Dwayne Eddie, almost all of these were terrible records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
